newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Luzhou Old-cellar seeks settlement on loan.
newsitem.headline: Luzhou Old-cellar seeks settlement on loan.

text.p: Shenzhen-listed distillery Luzhou Old-cellar Co Ltd said on Wednesday it is likely to have to repay part of a US$2.57 million loan it guaranteed several years ago, but was seeking an out-of-court settlement.

The Construction Bank of China has sued borrower Luzhou Construction Ceramics Factory and guarantor Luzhou Old-cellar for principal and interest totalling over US$3 million on a loan that matured in July, a spokesman at Old-cellar said.
The city of Luzhou, in southwest Sichuan province, had ordered Old-cellar to act as guarantor for the loan taken out by the ceramics plant in 1992, the spokesman said.

He said at that time, the distillery was a state-owned firm controlled by the city government, and that Old-cellar had been pressured into guaranteeing the loan regardless of the creditworthiness of the ceramics concern.
Old-cellar was restructured into a joint stock firm in 1994, but state shareholders still hold 75 percent in the firm.
The ceramics company is currently on the brink of bankruptcy, unable to repay the borrowings, the spokesman said.
He said the city was unlikely to assume liability for the loan, but that local officials had assured Old-cellar they would push for an out-of-court settlement.
